articles.title: ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract After Historic $1.6B Deal
articles.summary: ESPN has strongly denied an SEScoops report stating that it has already decided against renewing its five-year contract with WWE to be the exclusive American home for all Premium Live Events (PLEs).
articles.body:
ESPN has strongly denied an SEScoops report stating that it has already decided against renewing its five-year contract with WWE to be the exclusive American home for all Premium Live Events (PLEs).

Ben Cafardo of ESPN's Communications team released a statement on the matter, calling the rumors "categorically false."

Per CNBC's Alex Sherman , who cited people familiar with the deal back in Aug. 2025, ESPN is paying WWE an average of $325 million per year from 2026-2030.

ESPN Unlimited has shown WWE PLE's since Wrestlepalooza in Sept. 2025. That got the deal off to a big start, as the event featured John Cena, who was nearing the end of his retirement tour, taking on Brock Lesnar.

WWE has been promoted quite a bit on ESPN networks since the deal struck. All the biggest WWE events have appeared under the ESPN banner, including WrestleMania, SummerSlam and Royal Rumble.

WWE and ESPN appear to be all-in on this deal off the bat, and the one-year anniversary of the first PLE on ESPN Unlimited is rapidly approaching.

Ultimately, ESPN has clearly stated it's not looking for a way to back out. And in other news, three PLE's remain in 2026: Sunday Night's Main Event (Sept. 6), Money in the Bank (Oct. 10) and Survivor Series: WarGames (Nov. 28).

articles.title: González Fuertes sobre la jugada del Granada-Mallorca: "Estas cosas hacen mucho daño al estamento arbitral"
articles.standfirst: El exárbitro lamenta en Radio MARCA la polémica por el gol del Granada después de que se escuchara el pitido del colegiado tras el saque de esquina
articles.summary: El exárbitro lamenta en Radio MARCA la polémica por el gol del Granada después de que se escuchara el pitido del colegiado tras el saque de esquina
articles.body: Pablo González Fuertes fue protagonista en Radio MARCA para analizar algunas de las situaciones arbitrales que más dudas están generando en este inicio de temporada. El exárbitro se detuvo especialmente en la polémica del Granada-Mallorca, donde un gol quedó marcado por un pitido del colegiado que se produjo después de que el balón fuera golpeado en el saque de esquina. Además, aclaró y explicó con detalle la nueva normativa sobre cuándo los jugadores deben abandonar el terreno de juego después de recibir asistencia médica, y cómo funciona la nueva norma aplicada a los porteros. El exárbitro fue contundente con la acción del gol del Granada. El jugador puso el balón en juego y después se escuchó el silbato del colegiado. «El jugador atacante pone el balón en juego y posteriormente hay un sonido del silbato que invalidaría todo lo que pasa después», explicó. Para González Fuertes, lo más difícil de entender es que la jugada acabara en gol. «Lo que es inexplicable es que se dé gol», aseguró. Además, considera que la situación perjudica al colectivo arbitral: «Estas cosas no pueden pasar porque hacen mucho daño al estamento y a los compañeros». El excolegiado cree que había una solución sencilla para evitar la polémica: «Yo hubiese vuelto a pitar dos o tres veces, parar el partido y volver a reanudar el saque de esquina». González Fuertes defendió además que el arbitraje de élite requiere algo más que aplicar el reglamento. «Es saber gestionar situaciones complejas y saber darle una solución a esas situaciones», señaló. El VAR no podía corregir la acción porque el sonido del silbato no forma parte de los elementos revisables. «Esto no es una acción revisable por el VAR, porque el VAR no puede revisar audios», explicó. En la sala VOR no se escucha el sonido ambiente, sino únicamente las comunicaciones del equipo arbitral. Además, una imagen del árbitro con el silbato en la boca tampoco demuestra por sí sola que haya pitado: «Muchas veces te llevas el silbato en la boca y no pitas». Sobre una posible impugnación, González Fuertes lo encuadró como un error arbitral: «El error es intrínseco a nuestra profesión, hay que vivir con él», aunque reconoció que «hay errores que hacen más daño que otros». El exárbitro también explicó la norma sobre los futbolistas atendidos sobre el terreno de juego. «Todos los jugadores que son atendidos en el campo, en el que el cuerpo médico entra a atenderles, van a salir fuera y van a estar un minuto», indicó. La misma regla se aplica cuando el árbitro detiene el partido por una posible lesión. No ocurre, en cambio, si el jugador sale voluntariamente del campo para ser atendido o si ya estaba fuera cuando recibió la asistencia. Hay varias excepciones. Si el jugador atendido va a ser sustituido, el cambio se realiza inmediatamente. Tampoco debe salir si dos futbolistas del mismo equipo chocan, si va a lanzar un penalti o si acaba de recibir una falta por la que el rival ha sido amonestado o expulsado. En los golpes en la cabeza hay una casuística diferente. Si el árbitro detiene el juego, los jugadores deben salir, aunque si no necesitan asistencia pueden regresar inmediatamente. «Yo creo que esto lo van a cambiar, porque esto no tiene mucho sentido», reconoció González Fuertes. El objetivo de la nueva regla para los guardametas es evitar pérdidas de tiempo. Si un portero necesita atención, el entrenador tiene diez segundos para elegir a un compañero que permanezca un minuto fuera. Si no lo hace, será el capitán quien tenga que salir. Hay excepciones cuando existe una lesión evidente. «Si tú le pitas una falta al portero porque se acaba de llevar un golpe y le tienen que atender, pues no está perdiendo tiempo», explicó. Lo mismo sucede ante una hemorragia o una lesión grave: «No está perdiendo tiempo, pues ya no tiene por qué salir el compañero».

articles.title: Diego Pavia Makes Shocking U-Turn After Vanderbilt's Surprise QB Decision
articles.summary: Vanderbilt made a surprise move.
articles.body:
Diego Pavia just weighed in on Vanderbilt's quarterback decision. The former Commodores star backed the coaching staff. He applauded the choice of Blaze Berlowitz as the Week 1 starter.

College football reporter Pete Thamel shared the news on X, adding that Austin Peay will welcome the program's new starting quarterback.

Five-star freshman Jared Curtis will begin the season on the bench. Some might have expected the highly touted recruit to win the job immediately. Pavia took a different view.

He posted strong support for Berlowitz on social media.

"WELL EARNED- been watching this king from the start of time at NM STATE when he took over in the championship game at 18 years old and BALLED," Pavia wrote. "yall better stand down this man the truth!"

Berlowitz spent the last two seasons backing up Pavia. The two first teamed up at New Mexico State. Pavia knows exactly what his former teammate brings to the field.

He sees the decision as earned rather than a slight against Curtis. Berlowitz waited his turn and stayed ready. Pavia wants fans to respect that process.

Curtis remains a major talent. Pavia personally helped recruit the Nashville native to Vanderbilt. The former Heisman runner-up still believes in the freshman's future.

Pavia made clear his support is not a dig at Curtis. He simply celebrates a friend finally getting his shot. The senior has prepared for this moment across multiple seasons.

Vanderbilt opens against Austin Peay on September 5. Berlowitz will take the first snaps. Curtis will continue developing behind him. Pavia stands nearly alone in public approval of the call.

Diego Pavia continues to show loyalty to the program he helped transform. His message remains simple. Stand down and respect the player who earned the job.

articles.title: El Rayo abre la puerta a escuchar ofertas por Pathé Ciss
articles.standfirst: Raúl Martín Presa cambia el tono y acepta valorar propuestas por el internacional senegalés, que este martes acudió a la Ciudad Deportiva, pero no entrenó por segundo día consecutivo
articles.summary: Raúl Martín Presa cambia el tono y acepta valorar propuestas por el internacional senegalés, que este martes acudió a la Ciudad Deportiva, pero no entrenó por segundo día consecutivo
articles.body: El futuro de Pathé Ciss entra en días clave. El centrocampista del Rayo Vallecano ha acudido este martes a la Ciudad Deportiva, pero no se ha entrenado por segundo día consecutivo junto al resto de sus compañeros. El jugador mantiene firme su postura: quiere salir este verano porque considera que su ciclo en Vallecas está acabado. La situación ha provocado dos días de reuniones de mucha tensión entre las partes. Pathé lleva tiempo pidiendo al club que escuche las ofertas que han llegado por él. Hasta ahora, el Rayo se había mantenido cerrado en banda y se remitía a los 10 millones de euros de su cláusula. La novedad es que Raúl Martín Presa se ha mostrado por primera vez en los últimos años permeable a escuchar ofertas por el internacional senegalés. Un cambio de tono importante a falta de un año para la finalización de su contrato y después de que el futbolista haya decidido no ejercitarse con el grupo durante dos días consecutivos. El Rayo todavía no ha autorizado su salida, pero por primera vez acepta sentarse a valorar propuestas. La diferencia no es menor en una operación que venía bloqueada por la postura firme del club y por el deseo del jugador de iniciar una nueva etapa lejos de Vallecas. Pathé ha sido una pieza importante desde su llegada al Rayo en 2021, pero entiende que este verano debe marcar un punto de inflexión. Su contrato termina en 2027 y el club sabe que el margen para sacar rendimiento económico a una posible venta empieza a estrecharse. Los próximos días serán decisivos para comprobar si alguno de los clubes interesados transforma ese seguimiento en una propuesta capaz de convencer al Rayo. Besiktas y Al Shabab están atentos, también hay vías en España, y Pathé espera que esta vez el club sí se siente a escuchar. Después de años con la puerta cerrada, el escenario empieza a moverse.

articles.title: Red Sox Explain Adley Rutschman's Elbow Discomfort and Scheduled Day Off
articles.summary: Backup Boston Red Sox catcher Connor Wong will take over behind the plate for Adley Rutschman.
articles.body:
The Boston Red Sox decided to go all in at this year's trade deadline, sending a significant prospect package to the Baltimore Orioles for catcher Adley Rutschman .

Now in his fifth big-league season, Rutschman is already one of the most accomplished backstops of his era. He earned his third career All-Star selection this year and when available has excelled in all aspects of the game.

Across 79 games, the 28-year-old switch-hitting catcher has posted a .236 batting average, .320 on-base percentage, .726 OPS, nine home runs and 51 RBIs while continuing to play elite defense at a premium position.

Despite his track record, Rutschman's time in Boston is off to a slow start as he gets acclimated to his new team. He has also been gradually working his way back into a rhythm after spending time on the injured list.

At the time of the trade, Rutschman was sidelined with left wrist inflammation, which marked his third IL stint of the season alone.

Given how Rutschman has struggled to stay healthy, the Red Sox have routinely given him scheduled days off since his arrival. That figured to be the case for Tuesday's game against the Miami Marlins as Connor Wong took over behind the plate.

However, manager Chad Tracy announced the real reason when speaking with reporters during pregame.

Rutschman's removal was due to feeling discomfort in his right elbow, though Tracy did add that there is no concern, per Christopher Smith of MassLive.

Adley Rutschman took an aggressive swing yesterday and felt it a little in the right elbow. So Red Sox are just playing it safe with him today. Chad Tracy said there’s “no concern.” Just a scheduled day off for Caleb Durbin. Curtis Mead’s follow-up four-week scan showed enough… — Christopher Smith (@SmittyOnMLB) August 25, 2026

The Red Sox are going to be cautious with Rutschman given he is not just a rental piece. He is also under contract for the 2027 season, making his long-term health an organizational priority.

Rutschman will look to return to the starting nine on Wednesday for another game against Miami.

articles.title: Was Bronny James actually traded to the Sixers? What really happened
articles.summary: Some headlines suggested that Bronny James was traded.
articles.body:
When LeBron James opted to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers for the final stage of his legendary NBA career, there were obvious questions about what that meant for his son, Bronny James .

And there are some sites that are taking advantage of those questions.

Bronny was drafted by the Lakers in the second round in 2024 despite playing sparingly in one season at USC amid suffering cardiac arrest. The learning curve was always going to be steep for Bronny in the NBA, and LeBron's presence on the Lakers was the driving force behind Bronny ending up in Los Angeles .

But Bronny is still under contract with the Lakers and has not been traded .

Why are headlines claiming Bronny has been traded?

The website, TotalProSports, created a "trade proposal" blog but crafted a headline as if it was reporting a real trade. But the trade in question was total fiction.

By claiming that Bronny landed with the Sixers in a "blockbuster three-team trade," TotalProSports was able to fool search algorithms and use syndication agreements (such as with Yahoo! Sports ) to its advantage and get prominent placement.

It's a shady headline practice that is closer to lying than it is to creating content in good faith.

articles.title: ‘It’s all about her and only her’: Criticism mounts for Angel Reese after ‘selfish’ play
articles.summary: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are in the midst of a four-game winning streak, and on Monday night, in a win over the Los Angeles Sparks, Reese etched her...
articles.body:
Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are in the midst of a four-game winning streak, and on Monday night, in a win over the Los Angeles Sparks , Reese etched her name in the history books. Reese snagged a record-breaking 26 rebounds in the game, the most dominant performance on the glass in the WNBA's 30-year history.

Reese also recorded yet another double-double, scoring 11 points in the contest. However, the manner in which she scored her final bucket has been deemed "unethical" by some fans.

With the outcome already decided and less than 20 seconds remaining in regulation, Reese was camped out back at the Dream's basket rather than running back to defend with her teammates, which left her wide open to collect an outlet pass and reach double-digit scoring.

"We all know Angel Reese just wants her double double and look how she gets it. Cherry picking per usual. If she doesn't get to the free throw line or cherry pick, she can't score. It's all about her and only her," posted one person on X who wan't a fan of her tactics.

We all know Angel Reese just wants her double double and look how she gets it. Cherry picking per usual. If she doesn’t get to the free throw line or cherry pick, she can’t score. It’s all about her and only her. pic.twitter.com/DS0WlKPD8u — HeHateMe (@_HeHateMee_) August 25, 2026

We all know Angel Reese just wants her double double and look how she gets it.

Cherry picking per usual. If she doesn’t get to the free throw line or cherry pick, she can’t score. It’s all about her and only her. pic.twitter.com/DS0WlKPD8u

— HeHateMe (@_HeHateMee_) August 25, 2026

The original poster wasn't alone in his criticisms of Reese.

"Even half the time she does this she blows the layup and can't score. Shoots under 50% from within a couple ft of the basket. How's that even possible? Great rebounder but she's absolutely unskilled," one fan posted on X.

"Ahhh, now I can plainly see why she misses these layups. She jumps with both feet at the same time. Why hasn't this been corrected?" another fan wondered.

"What a low IQ and selfish play. Up 7 with 15 seconds left and she doesn't run the clock out?" someone else posted.

There's no denying that Reese's offensive game needs some polishing, but even so, her impact is undeniable. Reese is on a surefire path to ending up in the Hall of Fame, and with the Dream peaking right before the playoffs, she might even beat her rival Caitlin Clark to a WNBA championship.

The Little League World Series officially kicked off Wednesday, with the 20-team field finalized, featuring 10 U.S. teams and 10 international teams seeking a championship.

The tournament is back in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, once again this year, where all games will be held at Howard J. Lamade or Volunteer Stadium. Both the United States and International sides will play out double-elimination brackets until two teams from each bracket are left standing.

The remaining four teams will play in international and U.S. championship games on Aug. 29. The winner of those two games will advance to play in the championship game on Aug. 30. The losers of the semifinals will play in the third-place game.

articles.body: Carlos Slim, uno de los empresarios más influyentes de México, sigue sorprendiendo con los apoyos para las personas de nuestro país, ahora con la convocatoria de Becas 2026 de la Fundación Telmex Telcel, un programa que busca impulsar la preparación académica de estudiantes mexicanos. En esta edición, se contempla la entrega de 5 mil becas para quienes cursen una licenciatura, maestría o doctorado en instituciones educativas dentro de la República Mexicana. articles.title: Who has been the Bengals Preseason MVP?
articles.summary: It’s been a fun preseason for the Bengals, and guys like Colbie Young are a big reason why.
articles.body:
The preseason is nearly complete for the Cincinnati Bengals , who will face the Philadelphia Eagles on Friday night. After that, all 32 NFL teams will begin trimming down their rosters to 53 men before the deadline on August 30 at 6 PM ET.

For the Bengals, it's been a fun preseason thus far as they've rolled toward a 2-0 start, thanks in large part to several players who could be considered the team's MVP of the preseason.

So, we want you to tell us who has been the Bengals preseason MVP thus far.

Former CFL wide receiver Dohnte Meyers has been the surprise of camp and the preseason, going from facing an uphill climb just to make the practice squad to now likely securing a spot on the 53-man roster.

Fourth-round rookie Colbie Young has also been an impact pass-catcher and could be setting himself up to play meaningful snaps in Year 1.

On defense, seventh-round rookie Landon Robinson has been a pass-rushing force on the interior as he too looks to secure one of those final roster spots.

Edge rusher Isaiah Foskey has quietly racked up eight total pressures and a 77.0 PFF grade this preseason as he fights for one of the final edge spots.

Veteran linebacker and Super Bowl champion Swayze Bozeman has made some noise at linebacker and could sneak onto the 53-man roster when it's all said and done.

So, who would you crown the 2026 Bengals Preseason MVP thus far? Let us know your pick below!

Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bengals fans and fans across the country. And as always, WHO DEY!

articles.title: Warriors signing Georges Niang, Brandon Williams: How they fit with Golden State
articles.summary: The Warriors are signing Brandon Williams and Georges Niang to one-year deals. Here's how the players fit with Golden State.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors have had a rather quiet offseason that returned many familiar faces from last season's roster. Now, they have added two newcomers at the guard and forward positions.

The Warriors agreed to sign 6-foot-1 point guard Brandon Williams to a one-year, $2.6 million deal, according to ESPN NBA insider Shams Charania . Golden State also agreed to sign free agent forward Georges Niang to a one-year, $3.9 million deal, Charania reported.

Williams spent the 2025-26 season with the Dallas Mavericks , where he averaged career highs with 13 points and 3.9 assists in 66 games. Williams averaged 22.2 minutes per night, the most playing time he's seen since joining the NBA as an undrafted rookie signing in 2021.

Williams was on the Mavericks' roster the previous three seasons. He first entered the league playing for the Portland Trail Blazers , where he averaged 12.9 points in 24 games in 2021-22.

The veteran Niang has averaged 7.4 points per game across 544 NBA games, but did not play in 2025-26 due to injury.

The fifth-year NBA player joins a guard-heavy team already featuring the likes of Stephen Curry , Brandin Podziemski , Moses Moody , Will Richard , LJ Cryer , Gary Payton II and De'Anthony Melton.

Williams will seemingly be a spark off the bench for Golden State. It's a role Williams is familiar with and the Warriors know how dynamic he can be torching other second units − they got a taste of that work last season.

Williams had one of his best games against the Warriors on Christmas Day 2025, while with the Mavericks. Williams seemingly couldn't miss that day. He tallied 26 points on 9-for-12 shooting from the field.

He scored a career-high against the Memphis Grizzlies on March 7, 2025 when he went off for 31 points on 10-for-15 shooting, including 4-of-8 on 3-point field goals. He added six assists, five rebounds and a steal to his stat line. Williams showcased his ability to get to the rim and draw contact that game, getting to the free throw line eight times, making seven.

If healthy, Niang brings another 3-point shooting threat to the Warriors roster. He fits in all too well.

After a decade in the NBA, Niang has proved to be a reliable role player and credible 3-point shooter who connects from deep at a 40% clip for his career.

Niang missed the 2025-26 season due to a foot injury. The Warriors were all too familiar with injuries last season, with Curry, Moody, Jimmy Butler III and Al Horford among the big names impacted.

Niang has played for the Indiana Pacers , Utah Jazz , Philadelphia 76ers , Cleveland Cavaliers and Atlanta Hawks . He was going to return to the Jazz after a trade last offseason because the team felt his veteran presence would benefit their young core. Niang joining the Warriors' mix of veteran leadership and young reserves should be the perfect storm.

Plus, Niang should be somewhat familiar with the Warriors' organization and development system having played for their G-League affiliate, the Santa Cruz Warriors, during the 2017-18 season.

Williams won't have too much of a time getting acclimated with the Warriors and how they operate. He is already familiar with a member of the team.

Williams is a 26-year-old guard from Los Angeles . He attended Crespi Carmelite High School in Encino, California, where he was teammates with Melton. They dominated the floor when they shared the space. Melton averaged 20 points and Williams averaged 15.8 points as they led the Celts to a 33-5 record and won the CIF Division I state championship.

The two celebrated Williams' signing, posting a screen grab from their FaceTime video call showing both smiling as Williams quoted the tagline for hip-hop producer Chandler "Turbo" Durham.

"RUN IT BACK TURBOOOO @DeAnthonyMelton," Williams posted on X, formerly Twitter, with blue and yellow hearts symbolizing the Warriors' color-scheme.

RUN IT BACK TURBOOOO @DeAnthonyMelton 💛💙 pic.twitter.com/tyoarMA0R7 — Brandon Williams (@TheeBWill) August 25, 2026

RUN IT BACK TURBOOOO @DeAnthonyMelton 💛💙 pic.twitter.com/tyoarMA0R7

Although not Southern California, Williams is back on the West Coast, so that has to be a breath of fresh air for him. His familiarity with Melton should help make for a smooth transition to the Bay Area.

articles.title: Game Thread: Rangers (66-66) at White Sox (68-63)
articles.summary: Anthony Kay and the South Siders look to rebound from Monday’s rough loss
articles.body:
A blowout loss is a tough way to start a series at home in a playoff race, but the South Siders hope to flush Monday's game and come out strong behind Anthony Kay today. After defeating the Sox yesterday, the Rangers now hold a half-game lead over the Houston Astros in the AL West, while Chicago 's lead in the AL Central has shrunk to just 2 1/2 games over the Cleveland Guardians . The Guardians have rebounded from their rough stretch, winning seven of their last 10 and riding a five-game winning streak after defeating the Los Angeles Angels yesterday. The Angels, of course, had opportunities to come back but naturally didn't.

The South Siders are 5-5 in their last 10, and the offense has been struggling as a whole lately, basically living and dying by the long ball as we've seen in the last several games. In August, the White Sox are hitting just .208 with runners in scoring position as a team — the second-worst average in baseball over that stretch — while also racking up the most strikeouts (70). It also probably doesn't help that both Colson Montgomery and Munetaka Murakami are building Strikeout City from the ground up, with Colson leading MLB in Ks over the last two weeks (24 in 51 ABs) and Mune's 21 ranking third in baseball. Woof.

With both the rotation and bullpen continuing to struggle, the pitching staff took another hit when the White Sox announced that Huascar Brazobán is headed to the IL with a left lat strain. Righthander Jonathan Cannon is being called up from Triple-A Charlotte to help fill the hole. Jonathan Cannon is most certainly not the answer, but at this point, the front office seems ready to try anything.

Prior to tonight’s game vs. Texas, the Chicago White Sox placed right-handed pitcher Huáscar Brazobán on the 15-day injured list with a left lat strain and recalled right-handed pitcher Jonathan Cannon from Class AAA Charlotte. — Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) August 25, 2026

Prior to tonight’s game vs. Texas, the Chicago White Sox placed right-handed pitcher Huáscar Brazobán on the 15-day injured list with a left lat strain and recalled right-handed pitcher Jonathan Cannon from Class AAA Charlotte.

The only other roster update for today is that our sweet (mostly) clutch Andrew Benintendi has been placed on the bereavement list, and Rikuu Nishida will rejoin the team in his absence. We send our thoughts to Andrew and his family during this time.

Prior to tonight’s game vs. Texas, the Chicago White Sox placed outfielder Andrew Benintendi on the Bereavement/Family Medical Emergency List and recalled infielder/outfielder Rikuu Nishida from Class AAA Charlotte. — Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) August 25, 2026

Prior to tonight’s game vs. Texas, the Chicago White Sox placed outfielder Andrew Benintendi on the Bereavement/Family Medical Emergency List and recalled infielder/outfielder Rikuu Nishida from Class AAA Charlotte.

Regardless of what the masses may think, lefthander Anthony Kay has been solid for the Good Guys and is probably the second-best starter they currently have behind Sean Burke . Kay will make his 25th start of the season and has a 3.96 ERA and a 1.327 WHIP over 127 1/3 innings. He seems to keep improving, and in August alone, Kay has allowed just seven earned runs over 23 2/3 innings (four starts), good for a cool 2.66 ERA and a 2-1 record. If you ask me, his great outing against the Atlanta Braves last week went unrewarded because the offense was nowhere to be found.

Hopefully, the bats — or really anybody not named Miguel Vargas or Tristan Peters — can wake up to provide some early run support for Kay, but they will have a tough matchup with righthander Jacob deGrom on the mound. Peters has homered in three straight games, however, so let's see if he can make it four.

With Benintendi unavailable and a righty on the mound, Sam Antonacci is taking over as the DH and leading off today. Peters will shift to left field in Benintendi's place, while Brenton Doyle slots into center field and bats eighth. With those changes, today's lineup is almost identical to Monday's, and as we know, Will Venable loves the righty-lefty matchups. Still, I would be remiss not to mention Randal Grichuk 's career performance against deGrom: In 14 plate appearances, Grichuk has dominated. He's slashed .385/.429/1.000 with two home runs, amassing a 1.429 OPS.

deGrom is also making his 25th start of the season and holds a 3.77 ERA across 126 2/3 innings. The 38-year-old still has zero problems striking guys out and has rung up 157 batters this season. His 30.3% strikeout rate ranks in the top 8% of MLB pitchers. deGrom's fastball averages around 97 mph, though his off-speed pitches — slider, curveball and changeup — all fool batters, with all three pitches generating a whiff rate above 40%. His slider seems to be his most effective pitch, with opponents batting just .163 and slugging a measly .227 against it.

After being ejected from yesterday's game for heckling the ump, Joc Pederson will get another day off, with Justin Foscue remaining in the leadoff spot after a decent performance Monday. Corey Seager has been swinging a hot bat lately, and after two doubles and three RBIs yesterday, that is now apparent. In the past two weeks, Seager has the third-highest batting average in MLB (.419) and the sixth-highest OPS (1.164), and he's actually hit lefties better this year (.256 BA vs. .222 against righties).

First pitch is scheduled for 6:40 p.m. CDT, and it should be a beautiful night for a ballgame: 78º with partly cloudy skies. Watch on CHSN or listen on ESPN Chicago 1000 AM.

articles.summary: The O’s begin a nine-game road trip with a stop in St. Lous, where Chris Bassitt will toss the opener.
articles.body:
If the Orioles are going to make a push for the playoffs in this final month or so of the season, they are gonna have to win a bunch of games. That means beating solid teams like these Cardinals on the road. It's not gonna be easy.

It's a left-handed starter on the mound for St. Louis , Matthew Liberatore . That might be good news for the Orioles. They have been much improved against southpaws in recent months. As usual, Coby Mayo takes a prominent spot in the lineup, batting clean-up. He has a 1.105 OPS against lefties this year and has been pretty darn good overall in the second half, owning an .854 OPS since the all-star break.

Chris Bassitt will look to make it a third straight decent start since being activated from the IL. He has given up five runs over 11 innings since he returned from his back problems. After the off day on Monday the entire Orioles bullpen should be available, but it would still be nice to see Bassitt go a bit deeper here.

Let's start this nine-game road trip on a high note!

articles.title: Stevenage 0-3 Reading: Samba Rhythm Starts To Play
articles.summary: Jacob Brown, Paddy Lane and Randell Williams were on the scoresheet as Reading advanced to the third round of the League Cup.
articles.body:
"As the samba rhythm starts to play, dance with me, make me sway…"

So goes Paddy Lane 's chant. It's been sung out of optimism more than expectation in the year or so since he joined – the former Portsmouth winger struggling to show us what he's capable of on a consistent basis.

But tonight, at long last, this was absolutely Lane's night. It wasn't just about a single dramatic moment though, like when he netted winners last season over Port Vale or Bradford City. Rather, this was the kind of game that made you think that a big talent – one with so much potential to offer – may now have truly found his feet.

Would the Lane of last season have sent in that accurate low cross for Jacob Brown to convert for 1-0? Would he have cheekily lobbed Filip Marschall for 2-0? Football often comes down simply to being about confidence, and Lane demonstrated plenty of that throughout this evening's game.

But this was a pleasingly confident display all round from the Royals, who are now properly up and running for the season, and have a spot in the third round of the League Cup to look forward to. Although penalty shootout success is a victory of sorts, and we'd managed two of those already this season, tonight was Reading's first proper win.

And what better way to get it than in this kind of style? Three good goals from open play scored, none conceded (for the second match in a row) and a convincing attacking display that bore all the hallmarks of what Leam Richardson was trying to build over the summer: quick, direct and quality wide play.

The goals themselves were great examples of that. The first: a low cross from a winger (Lane setting up Brown). The second: a goal put away by a winger (Lane). The third: a winger putting the ball on a plate for another winger at the back post (Kyreece Lisbie, albeit playing up front in a 3-5-2, passing for Williams).

Not just a good performance then, but everything (as far as I can tell) going to plan. That samba rhythm wasn't confined just to Lane after all.

Richardson made nine changes from Saturday's 0-0 draw at AFC Wimbledon, with Joel Pereira and Benn Ward the only survivors. Conor Masterson and George Earthy were given full debuts, while there were also a number of first-team players included on a strong-looking bench.

Reading (4-2-3-1): Pereira; Ahmed, Masterson, Ward, Dorsett ; Fraser, Savage; Williams, Earthy, Lane; Brown Subs: Stevens, Roberts, Wing, Rinomhota, Stokes, Osho, Kyerewaa, Lisbie

Reading (4-2-3-1): Pereira; Ahmed, Masterson, Ward, Dorsett ; Fraser, Savage; Williams, Earthy, Lane; Brown

Subs: Stevens, Roberts, Wing, Rinomhota, Stokes, Osho, Kyerewaa, Lisbie

After a slightly shaky start in the early moments of the game, when debutant Masterson had to be on his toes, Reading took a 0-1 lead in the ninth minute. Liam Fraser pinged the ball out wide to Lane on the the left, whose low cross to the near post was diverted in by Brown.

The Royals played with confident at this point and looked to push for a second. The pairing down the right of full-back Ashqar Ahmed and winger Williams was a particularly potent-looking one, just as it had been in pre-season at Crawley Town.

A quarter of an hour or so after the opener, Reading doubled their lead. This time a long ball down the left wasn't dealt with properly by a Stevenage defender, whose loose header dropped for Lane. He still had a fair amount to do to beat the onrushing 'keeper, but dinked the ball over Marschall and home for 0-2 .

There was no other major action in the remainder of a positive half. The Royals generally looked bright in possession and did well enough to restrict a fairly limited attacking effort from the hosts, with Pereira not called into any heroics.

The second 45 was, on the whole, a much more even affair than the first, with the hosts coming fairly close to finding a way back into the game a few times.

That started off pretty early as Stevenage managed to put the Royals' defence under extended pressure soon after the restart. They even had the ball in the net not long after the interval, tucking it home from a deep free-kick on their left – but thankfully from an offside position.

Around 10 minutes later, more opportunities came Stevenage's way. Pereira did well to parry a powerful shot from the edge of the area on one occasion, and soon after watched a header (set up by a cross from our right) go wide of the post.

Down the other end though, Reading were carrying a threat going forwards of their own. This was a crucial difference from previous games this season, in which the Royals had looked good in the first half but struggled to maintain offensive consistency in the second.

The first example of that was a smart run in behind from Earthy a few minutes after the restart, getting on the edge of a Brown flicked header before forcing a save at the near post. The summer signing had other opportunities midway through the half – both of them being shots blocked inside the Stevenage area.

Reading seemed to be fading somewhat in the last 20 minutes, with the hosts in the ascendancy. The Royals' inability to kill the game off earlier in the half perhaps emboldened the home side, who piled more and more pressure on the visitors.

Richardson made his first change in the 81st minute, swapping Earthy off for Lisbie. That also meant a switch to a 3-5-2: Lane slotting in as a left-wing-back as the back four shunted over, with Williams going into midfield and Lisbie partnering Brown up front.

Ward then almost inadvertently helped Stevenage to halve the deficit. A low cross from Stevenage's left ricocheted off the defender inside the six-yard area, towards goal, but fortunately Pereira was able to block the ball.

Nervy times indeed, but Reading soon killed the game. Brown picked the ball up in space, slipped Lisbie in behind with a cute pass, and his low cross to the back post set up one of the easiest finishes Williams will have in his career. 0-3 , job done.

With the match killed off, Richardson made one more change. Lane was given a well deserved standing ovation from a jubilant away end as he was replaced by Daniel Kyerewaa – whose spot in the first team he could well soon take.

So, at the fifth time of asking, Reading finally have a normal-time win in 2026/27. What's more, we've got a mini cup run on our hands, and hopefully we'll have an exciting draw in the next round to look forward to.

Besides the obvious morale boost of a good performance and comfortable scoreline, Richardson will also be pleased with a few aspects of the Royals' performance: ruthlessness with chances, more consistent attacking threat across the 90 minutes, quality from out wide, not collapsing after the break, riding out the pressure Stevenage offered, and squad players staking a convincing claim to regular minutes in the league.

All in all then, surely exactly the kind of performance Richardson has been trying to establish in the last few months. The tricky next step: getting Reading to do this regularly in the league.

articles.title: IndyCar’s Freedom 250 Grand Prix Promoter: ‘This Is My Sistine Chapel’
articles.summary: IndyCar's Freedom 250 Grand Prix Of Washington DC was an epic spectacle in the Nation's Capital. Forbes Sports Money provides a behind-the-scenes look at the...
articles.body:
There is a slogan in auto racing that best exemplifies the unbelievable 60-year success of Team Penske and Roger Penske's incredible accomplishments in business.

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington DC was a perfect example of that slogan because Penske and IndyCar were able to create a sporting event in the National Mall of Washington, DC that was so stunning, so magical, and so well-orchestrated that it is hard to put it into words to someone who wasn't on the grounds.

It was the first auto racing ever held on the historic streets that surround the National Mall. Penske Corporation President Bud Denker was the man responsible for taking an impossible task and turning it into a moment of pride for IndyCar, the 150,000 spectators and 3,282,000 viewers that watched on FOX.

"I've never been on a journey like this in my life," Denker told me after the race. "I've been in a lot of deals, been in a lot of decisions. Been in a lot of sponsorship deals that were incredibly big, but I just can't ever imagine doing anything bigger than this.

"The Sistine Chapel was probably the most amazing thing that happened for Leonardo da Vinci.

Freedom 250 Grand Prix Gets Biggest Viewership For A Non-Indy 500 in Decades

It was the most-viewed non-Indy 500 race since the start of the IndyCar Series when the Indy Racing League and Champ Car merged before the 2008 season. It was up 364 percent over last year's 708,000 viewers for the FOX portion of last year's 15 th race from Portland, when the first 31 minutes started on FS1.

Sunday's viewership was up 279 percent with last year's 867,000 viewers for Sunday non-Indy 500 races on FOX.

The race partially overlapped with the NASCAR Cup race from New Hampshire which ran on USA from 2:14-6:36 pm.

The full race telecast averaged 1,686,000 viewers and the race peaked with 3,482,000 viewers from 2:30-2:45pm.

IndyCar on FOX is averaging 1,875,000 viewers through 15 races, up 32 percent vs. last year's season to date of 1,416,000 and up 70 percent over the 2024 season to date when 1,106,000 for races on NBC/USA/CNBC.

It was IndyCar's gift to the 250 th Birthday of the United States, but the positive reaction from those that came from around the world to witness the race may be IndyCar's biggest gift. Many of those fans had never attended an auto race before. Some left the race saying they were now IndyCar fans.

Freedom 250 On Track Action Driving Reaction

From a racing standpoint, Kyle Kirkwood dominated, winning the race after leading 128 laps of the 147-lap contest. There was plenty of action, though, throughout the field with 155 passes during the contest.

"It was racy. You could pass," said third-place finisher Will Power of Andretti Global. "A lot of my positions were gained just on-track passes. It was everything you'd want. Having an American President here watching the whole race, still there when I pulled up on the grid, you could see President Trump still watching, which meant that the race must have been pretty engaging, which is really good stuff. Great for the series."

I asked Power had what point in the day the moment of the magnitude of this spectacle hit him?

"Probably when we jumped in the truck and drove around," Power said. "You see the pageantry. It had a very Indy 500 vibe.

"I think IndyCar is in the best shape it's ever been in since I've been in the series. That's 21 years. It's just progressively gone up. More recently it's taken a big step. Really proud to be a part of it."

While some fans may look at the same driver leading 128 laps in front of the field with a negative reaction, the value of this event wasn't necessarily what happened on the track, it was having IndyCar as the star attraction for a huge crowd in a setting unlike any other.

It wasn't the Indianapolis 500, where 350,000 fans jam the Indianapolis Motor Speedway for the world's most famous and historic race. But for a street race near the end of the summer celebrating a milestone moment in the history of the United States that drew 150,000 enthusiastic fans, it was a major event for both IndyCar and the USA.

"This morning when I woke up, quite honestly, there's an instinct that you have when you wake up and your heart is already racing," the race-winner said. "I only get that one other place, and that's the Indy 500. Just that sensation, it gives it its own energy. That's what this place had.

"This was a very special day. We were very prepared for it. Outside of the Indy 500, I don't think there's another race that you'd want to win."

Freedom 250 Grand Prix One Last Celebration Of The 250th Birthday Of The United States

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, DC was historic for where it was being held. The US Capitol Building in the background behind the flag stand and other iconic structures such as the National Archives, the Washington Monument, the National Archives and other famed attractions made it a spectacular setting.

Every branch of the United States Military was honored with each branch's marching band performing on the track. There were seven military flyovers during the event including the B2 Stealth Bomber and a special flyover from Air Force One escorted by F-15 Eagles and F-15 Fighting Falcons.

Freedom 250 Grand Prix Was IndyCar's American Dream

Denker and his team were able to create a spectacle out of something many critics didn't believe would ever happen. He started a lengthy lobbying effort that began in August 2025 with 81 meetings on Capitol Hill trying to get it approved by the United States House of Representatives and US Senate.

On January 21, the project was at an impasse. There wasn't enough support to get approval for the areas of the National Mall that were required to put up a temporary street circuit.

Denker told Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy that he was pulling the plug, that the race wouldn't happen. Duffy encouraged Denker to hold off because he had another plan.

He was able to get an Executive Order from President Donald J. Trump on January 30.

That's when the hard work began to plan the event, and secure the proper permits and licenses required because of all the different jurisdictions involved.

"If you asked anybody in this town, or I would say on our industry, could we have a race in Washington, D.C. a year ago, the answer would have been, 'are you crazy?'" Denker told me. "That is what most of them said when I first came up here a year ago.

"But I didn't think it was a crazy idea.

"Resiliency, I think, is the key word for me. Persistence is the other piece. And don't take no, because there are a lot of 'no's' here.

"People have this phrase, 'Penske Perfect.' We're never perfect, but we're not going to have people think we are. That's pretty good to me, and many people thought this was perfect. And for a first -time event, my team made a flawless execution."

Although he is the Penske Corporation President and works out of the corporate offices near Detroit, Denker spent most of his time living in Washington, DC beginning last August. He was running solo until March, trying to put the event together.

"Remember, my team also had to do the IndyCar race at Arlington as a first-time event in March," Denker explained. "Jonathan Bailey was running the operations at Arlington and then they had to do the Chevrolet Detroit Grand Prix in June, so I was borrowing resources wherever I could.

"Most of it was me initially to get the organization to meet all the people, all the stakeholders I had to meet with. 50-plus stakeholders that surround this track, multiple meetings, greasing the skids before these guys got here."

Freedom 250 Work Kicked Into High Gear In June

Denker said it the race was really put together with his full team beginning in June, which meant it had to be ready to go in a little over two full months.

"It's an interesting city because we're in John Hopkins University right now, but the sidewalk outside is owned by the National Park Service," Denker explained. "The curb across the street is owned by the National Art Gallery, and the street is owned by the city of Washington, DC. Down about 50 yards, that area is owned by the National Archives. Further up the road, that walkway is owned by the Smithsonian Institute.

"And then you have all of the Capitol grounds. We can't touch the Capitol on the curb, because that would violate the president's executive order.

"All of these entities, we had to deal with to put things together, 1,350 pages it permits. To weld a manhole cover here, you need a big, big, big, thick page of permits. We couldn't wash the track here like we do everywhere else. We couldn't wash the track because we couldn't wash water into the drainage areas here, despite the fact that rain goes down those drainage areas as well.

"So those are just complexities that you have to do here. But despite that, we got through it all, and we have great partnerships with the city, and 1,350 pages of permits is a lot."

Denker was all over the property leading up to the race and rode in one of the Presidential Limousines on a ceremonial lap. Afterwards, Denker and Penske watched the contest in the Presidential Suite along with the President and First Lady.

Could The Freedom 250 Grand Prix Return to Washington DC In The Future?

President Trump, Washington, DC Mayor Muriel Bowser and many other government officials want the Freedom 250 Grand Prix to be back on the IndyCar schedule in future years. But this race was originally created as a one-time-only event to help celebrate the 250 th birthday of the United States.

The Penske Corporation invested $35 million to make this event happen. Although 150,000 fans came on Sunday with 214,000 fans for the two-day weekend, tickets were free and distributed through a lottery system from the 288,000 requests that were submitted.

Revenue came from the sale of lavish VIP suites and from an impressive list of corporation sponsors. Merchandise sales were impressive with lines of spectators buying up all the Freedom 250 Grand Prix merchandise they could find. According to Denker, $900,000 of merchandise was sold on Saturday alone. At the Grand Prix of Arlington, $900,000 of merchandise was sold over the weekend for a first-time event.

For it to become an annual event, the business structure would have to generate significant revenue.

"We have a difficult choice to make," Denker said. "The question is this. How many people would come back again for the event in Year Two, a non-anniversary year for the United States? Could you charge tickets, a price for tickets, to cover some of the revenue and the loss you have because this is so expensive? Is it $50 a person? What would that do to the crowd?

"Or did you tease them enough this year enough this year that they really would want to come back and would come back also by paying something that's reasonable?

"That's the questions we have to look at. And I think the key thing for us is to probably talk to our sponsors and say, is there interest in coming back?

"But ultimately, it's a Roger Penske decision. We'll make that decision pretty soon."

Denker sat with Penske and his wife, Kathy, in the Presidential Suite throughout the race and expressed his appreciation and gratitude for what the event meant to him and his family.

"This is my crowning achievement," Denker said. "Roger has had a lot of crowning achievements in his life, many more than I have, but it won't get better for me. I know this is one of the top ones for Roger."

This event was about Patriotism, and the fans that came to the race were happy to be part of the celebration and turned the National Mall into one of the "happiest places on Earth" at least for one day.

Roger Penske Thanks Freedom 250 Fans With A Special Full-Page Letter In The Washington Post

Penske showed his appreciation to the fans by taking out a full-page ad in The Washington Post on Tuesday with the following letter:

"To Our Fans, Thank you for making the Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C., such an extraordinary and memorable event for our nation.

"The energy and enthusiasm you brought to our nation's capital made this weekend truly special. Whether you joined us in Washington or watched from home, your passion for INDYCAR and motorsports was on full display and helped create a celebration worthy of America's 250th anniversary.

"We are grateful to President Trump and his Administration for their leadership and support in making this historic event possible. We also thank Mayor Bowser and the broader team in Washington, D.C., for their partnership and for working together with our organization to bring the Freedom 250 Grand Prix to life in our Nation's Capital.

"The Freedom 250 Grand Prix brought together the speed, competition and pageantry of INDYCAR racing with an incredible celebration of our country. Seeing the cars race through Washington, surrounded by iconic landmarks and thousands of fans, created images and memories that will stay with all of us for years to come.

"I also want to thank all of our INDYCAR drivers and teams for delivering an outstanding weekend of competition and congratulate Kyle Kirkwood on his victory in the Freedom 250 Grand Prix.

"Motorsports has always been about more than the cars on the track. It is about the fans, the teams, the drivers, our partners and the many people behind the scenes who make our sport possible. This weekend was a tremendous example of what can be accomplished when people come together around a shared vision.

"Our partners at FOX played an important role in bringing that experience to millions of viewers across the country. Their commitment to INDYCAR has helped showcase our drivers, teams and racing to a growing audience, and we are proud to have them as a partner.

"We are also grateful to the many brands and partners whose support helped make this historic event possible, including Monumental Sports & Entertainment and Harbinger. Their commitment and collaboration were instrumental in bringing this ambitious vision to life.

"As we celebrate America's 250th anniversary, all of us at INDYCAR are incredibly proud to have played a part in this historic occasion.

"Most importantly, thank you again to our fans. Your passion is what drives our sport forward, and we could not be prouder to have shared this unforgettable celebration of America and INDYCAR with you.

"Roger Penske, Chairman of Penske Entertainment"

It's likely the Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington DC may be the only time a street race is held in the Nation's Capital on the streets around the National Mall. It certainly provided a "Once in a Lifetime" event for those who attended, giving Denker and his team his "Sistine Chapel" moment.

articles.summary: La conductora señaló que había cumplido una etapa en su carrera
articles.body: Un par de semanas después de anunciar de manera sorpresiva su salida de TUDN, la conductora Valeria Marín finalmente reveló los motivos por los que decidió no continuar en Televisa después de la cobertura de la Copa del Mundo y también aclaró los rumores de su salida y una supuesta relación con el analista de esa misma cadena deportiva, Marc Crosas. Recordemos que hace un par de semanas, tras el anuncio de su salida de TUDN, comenzaron a circular varias versiones sobre las razones por las que no continuará en Televisa, entre ellas, se habló de una petición de aumento de sueldo, que habría provocado que tomará la decisión de no continuar luego de 7 años en esa empresa. Valeria Marín llegó a TUDN hace 7 años y señaló que después de pensarlo y cerrar la cobertura de la Copa del Mundo tomó la decisión de salir de la cadena deportiva y además aseguró estar contenta de haber dado un paso al costado. "Después del Mundial, después de pensarlo, dije 'me despido con una cobertura increíble', yo creo que ya hice lo que tenía que hacer en este lugar, el lugar también me dio lo que me tenía que haber dado o lo que me gané y sería bonito cerrarlo en lo más alto. Estoy súper feliz con la decisión que tomé y muy emocionada por lo que se pueda venir". Estas declaraciones las hizo en el podcast 'Sabor a Fútbol', en donde también hizo referencia un par de veces a su pareja, el actor Julián Gil quien según las palabras de la conductora le dio un par de consejos antes de tomar la decisión de salir de TUDN: "Me dijo ' no pongas todos los huevos en la misma canasta', y sí, estoy dejando a la televisora más fuerte en México pero ver que hay un mundo mucho más grande, en donde puedes tener muchas más opciones Desde luego uno de los puntos más atractivos del poscast fue cuando hablaron sobre los rumores que rodearon su salida de TUDN, incluido un aparente romance con el panelista Marc Crosas y también el aumento de sueldo que derivó en la decisión que tomó: "Yo di todo, ellos me dieron todo. Yo quiero más como cualquier profesional, siempre aspiramos a más, quizás el canal no me lo puede dar". Y cuando se le preguntó sobre la relación que algunos rumores instalaron con su compañero en TUDN, respondió a manera de broma: "Confieso que somos pareja swinger, Marc si entra en la ecuación pero salgo de la cancha yo y entre Marc, entonces son 'Juli' y Marc", al tiempo en el que comenzó a reírse, "esas veriones ni las aclaro y dan risa, la gente no está preparada para esta conversación".

articles.body:
Can the Hoosiers win back-to-back national championships? College football analyst Paul Finebaum does not think so. In fact, after making a bold prediction about it, he received online backlash.

Now, he's come back and doubled down on his take.

Paul Finebaum Reiterates 2026 Bold Prediction for Indiana Hoosiers

Finebaum didn't mince words with his recent bold prediction regarding the Hoosiers. After a fairy-tale season a year ago, Finebaum says people need to chill out on Indiana in 2026.

The college football analyst recently said Indiana is not winning the national championship this season, and plenty of people came after him for that take.

On Tuesday, he got a chance to respond on "First Take," and he took the opportunity to double down.

"I am not taking back a single thing. Maybe I could have said it nicer. Maybe I could have been more diplomatic," Finebaum said . "I didn't know a single Indiana graduate until midway through last season, and now they are literally falling out of Amazon trucks. I don't know what's going on here."

Finebaum predicted the Hoosiers would finish the regular season 10-2 and make the playoffs, but doesn't have belief in Indiana past that point.

"I think Indiana is a really good team. I predicted they'll go to the playoffs. They're probably 10-2. I'm worried about their offensive line," Finebaum said. "Worried about the secondary. Worried about the quarterback. Yes, the schedule, which I went into.

"I can't wait to hear you brag a little bit more because your time of bragging is about over."

PREDICT THE CFB SEASON: PFN's Free CFB Playoff Predictor

Finebaum's last sentence was targeted at "First Take" host Shae Cornette, who is an Indiana graduate.

While Finebaum doesn't believe the Hoosiers will go back-to-back, he doesn't think the program's run last season was a fluke. Curt Cignetti certainly started something at Indiana, and many believe he'll keep it going for years to come.

However, the Hoosiers had a lot of moving parts this offseason, with players heading to the NFL, led by Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza.

MORE: 'One of the Worst College Football Coaches I Have Ever Seen' — Paul Finebaum Ethers Bill Belichick Amid UNC's 'Mass Chaos'

They had to be active in the transfer portal, and they were. But getting all of those new pieces to work together is easier said than done.

According to PFN's College Football Power Rankings , the program enters the program as the No. 3-ranked team in the country with a 27.50 rating, trailing only Ohio State (28.75) and Oregon (27.75).

articles.title: WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Heatwave 2026
articles.summary: On the week ahead of Heatwave, NXT presented a final show on August 25 in the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida.
articles.body:
On the week ahead of Heatwave, NXT presented a final show on August 25 in the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida.

As part of a Championship Summit, Tony D'Angelo would meet his future challengers Grayson Waller, Cruz Montana and Zilla Fatu while Kendal Grey exchanged final words with Kelani Jordan.

Saquon Shugars and Dion Lennox opened the show in a Weaponized Steel Cage. EK Prosper challenged Rey Fénix for the AAA Cruiserweight Championship.

This was only the foundation of an important night. Check out all the results, grades and highlights for NXT below.

Weaponized Steel Cage: Saquon Shugars vs. Dion Lennox

Last Time in Action: Dion Lennox defeated Saquon Shugars (NXT, August 11).

Lennox tossed a trash can at Shugars as he entered the cage, starting an immediate brawl. Lennox relied on his surroundings early, tossing Shugars repeatedly into the steel.

Shugars found a way to fire back, trapping Lennox in a trash can which he attacked with a trash can lid and Missile Dropkick.

Lennox fought free and dropped Shugars' back onto a chair into the Picture-in-Picture break.

Out of the break, Lennox fired up, tossing Lennox into the cage and flying out of the corner with a fast Crossbody.

He whipped Lennox into a kendo stick followed by face-planting Lennox into a steel chair. Lennox responded with a Spinebuster onto a trash can for a near-fall.

Lennox began targeting the leg of Shugars, using a steel chair and Shugars' own bat to target the left knee.

Shugars tried to send Lennox through a table with a Sunset Flip Powerbomb, but his knee gave out.

Shugars kept fighting through the limp and, in a final desperation move, went all the way to the top of the cage for a Crossbody to seal the win.

This was by far the best these two have looked in singles action, especially against one another.

Plunder matches especially with this many pre-set weapons gave them the structure their standard matches lacked.

The aggression of Lennox is far more effective when he is swinging chairs and tossing his opponent into a cage than utilizing his standard offense.

He also showed some impressive ingenuity throughout, combining weapons with the cage that sold his intellect.

This match also gave Shugars a chance to lean into his ability to sell pain, highlighting his resilience while the crowd cheered him on.

The ending was hampered by an early table break, but Shugars soldiered through and still hit a nice top-of-the-cage Crossbody, even if it did not look as devastating as they originally planned.

This should be the end of the rivalry for now. Shugars does not need to go through Osiris Griffin and Cutler James. He just needs to move on.

Let Shugars start building a resume that can allow him to challenge for the North American Championship while DarkState finds a new target.

Booker T oddly clarified that Shugars and Lennox don't hate each other. They just have "bad blood".

Vic Joseph explained that this could have been on Heatwave, but Robert Stone did not believe these two could wait. Booker again oddly questioned if this would have made the premium live event card.

"Use the Table" is a new obnoxious chant the NXT audience provided in place of "We Want Tables".

Shugars Superkicked Lennox after trapping him in a trash can on top of a table, only for the table to break early before the finish.

Nattie and Jaida Parker Agree to a Submission Match at Heatwave

Jaida Parker asked Thea Hail to stay in the back before she headed to the ring to face down Nattie.

The Low-Key Legend explained that she came to NXT to fight Ms. Parker, but she saw a Jaida that had grown soft and failed in her potential.

Jaida called out that Nattie tried to break her, but she only fired up a woman that was ready to embarrass her.

The two agreed to fight at Heatwave in a Submission match.

It is far too rare in the NXT women's division to see two stars just talk without interruption, especially without it quickly turning to violence.

That made this fairly basic promo stand out. Ms. Parker rode a supportive crowd to talking her way through Nattie, selling her confidence.

Even though The Low-Key Legend is the favorite on paper in this type of match, Jaida came out of this selling that there is no way that Nattie could make her tap out again.

Jaida should win against Nattie, and this win should set her up to take the next step to gold in NXT. She is ready for bigger opportunities.

In a backstage interview, Tony D'Angelo ran down all his challengers, promising none of them were ready for his fight.

The Vanity Project met Sarah Schreiber at a bowling alley where they called Myles Bornes and Tavion Heights fake friends while talking up Myka Lockwood as their secret weapon.

Last Time in Action: Kam Hendrix defeated Mason Rook (NXT, August 11); Keanu Carver defeated EK Prosper (NXT, August 4).

Carver teased an early inside cradle then took the best offense of Hendrix and smiled. The Showtime Kick could not even keep Carver down for two.

A pair of Release German Suplexes followed by a Pounce sent Hendrix to the floor. Showtime poked Carver in the eye, but as the referee talked to Carver, Mason Rook laid out Hendrix with a Running Crossbody.

Carver followed up with a Bridging Fisherman Suplex for the victory.

The positive was that Carver looked great. He shrugged off Hendrix's best offense and showed off a growing variety of moves in his arsenal.

It feels like Carver has fully landed in NXT, and his natural growth in the company makes him an easy choice to win gold soon.

The negative was a rushed and flat finish that made out that Carver needed Rook's help to seal the win in a match he was dominating.

It also was noticeable that Carver and Hendrix are a bad pair with limited in-ring chemistry. This is definitely not a match to quickly revisit.

Hendrix can continue feuding with Rook while Carver should look to the champions that leave Heatwave with the gold.

While big names are challenging Tony D'Angelo, Carver feels like a better long-term bet for NXT as a future NXT champion.

NXT showed footage of Carver finding out last minute that he would fight Hendrix. Carver teased anger but gladly accepted the challenge.

The crowd did not know how to react in this impromptu heel vs. heel match, but Carver won them over more, signaling he might be slowly turning.

In a pre-tape, Zilla Fatu promised to make a splash immediately in NXT.

Last Time in Action: Kali Armstrong alongside Kelani Jordan defeated WrenQCC (NXT, August 18); Zaria defeated Wren Sinclair to defend the Women's North American Championship (NXT, August 11).

Zaria and Kali began quickly testing each other's strength. The women's North American champion was too much for the former Evolve women's champion.

Instead of strength though, it was speed that gave Kali an edge as she knocked Zaria outside and caught her with a Springboard Crossbody into the PIP break.

Back from break, Kali kept control with an explosive Superplex. The two exchanged strikes in the center of the ring that ended with Kali standing tall.

Kali set up the Kali Connection, but Zaria countered into a Spear followed by an F5, only for Kali roll through into a Sunset Flip pin for the shock victory.

This was a great showcase for Kali. Zaria let the NXT newcomer look like a real threat by pushing Kali to her most dynamic performance on NXT so far.

This was not just a showcase of the explosive power of Kali. It was instead about the dynamic athleticism of one of NXT's most intriguing rising stars.

Kali did not need to actually beat Zaria, who has been well protected lately, but she will add more unpredictability to the Heatwave Unification match.

The best bet is for Zaria to take all the gold, but Kali is also a priority star in NXT. Zaria could easily go after the NXT Championship instead.

Kali def. Zaria by pinfall to earn a spot in the Heatwave championship unification match.

In a pre-tape, Kelani Jordan talked about how she has done everything in NXT and been disrespected constantly.

Kendal Grey talked with Wren Sinclair and NASCAR racer William Sawalich about doctor concerns about her balance for her title match against Lani.

BirthRight vs. Sean Legacy, DVD, Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno

Last Time in Action: This was the last time Lexis King, Charlie Dempsey, Channing "Stacks" Lorenzo and Uriah Connors have teamed up as a foursome since NXT Countdown to Stand & Deliver (April 4). This was the first time Sean Legacy, Dorian Van Dux, Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno have worked as a foursome.

The action quickly picked up as BirthRight could not contain the speed and ferocity of Legacy, DVD, Dar and Romeo.

Connors managed to trip up Romeo though, pulling him outside and face-planting him on the floor into the commercial break.

BirthRight continued to dominate Romeo back from break until Romeo managed to flip past everyone to DVD hot tag.

Dux dived onto BirthRight then tagged in Legacy to set up a Springboard 450 on Stacks, but King broke up the pin.

Dempsey and Dar tagged in before the babyfaces began an explosive comeback, diving onto the field. In the chaos, Dempsey caught The Scottish Supernova with a Bridging Regalplex for the victory.

This was a formulaic tag team match but continued to highlight the impressive rising athletes in NXT's undercard.

In particular, DVD and Romeo were flying with fire throughout, creating a whole new highlight reel of moves just from this contest.

It would have been nice to see BirthRight do more than just survive though given their significant experience advantage as a unit.

Instead, it just felt like Dempsey survived by out-wrestling Dar one-on-one in the last minute, which does not do much for BirthRight as a team.

Still, at least the right group won for the moment, hopefully setting up more focused matches for the future between these groups.

One of the babyfaces in this match should be the one to finally dethrone Lexis King as Men's Speed champion.

Dempsey, King, Stacks and Connors def. Dar, Romeo, Legacy and DVD by pinfall.

Booker T questioned who the leader of BirthRight is. Vic Joseph assumed it was Lexis King, but it is odd that has not been established five months in.

DVD was the biggest crowd favorite in this match, and his explosive offense paid off that support.

Backstage, Keanu Carver reminded an annoyed Robert Stone that the referee's decision is final while Shiloh Hill asked for a match with Naraku next week.

AAA World Cruiserweight Championship: Rey Fénix (c) vs. EK Prosper

Last Time in Action: Rey Fénix defeated Dragon Lee to advance to the finals of the World Heavyweight Championship No. 1 Contender Tournament (Raw, August 24); EK Prosper defeated La Parka, Romeo Moreno and Tristan Angels (NXT, August 18).

Despite a confident start from Fénix, Prosper flipped through the grip of the champion and sent him to the floor with a Dropkick.

He followed up with a Moonsault to the floor to send this match into a commercial break.

The champion fired back out of the break, only to get countered again by Prosper including a Springboard Leg Drop for a near-fall.

Fénix fired back with Adios Amigo into a Diving Crossbody and Frog Splash for his own near-fall.

Prosper countered a Rolling Cutter with a Suplex but bounced the champion into a Handspring Cutter. Prosper blocked the Mexican Muscle Buster and planted the champion with a Top-Rope Headscissors.

Fénix dodged the Moonsault followed by a Corner Enzuigiri, Superkick and Mexican Muscle Buster for the win.

Despite positioning this as the epic main event of NXT, it never truly felt like Prosper was ready for the spotlight given to him.

Fénix is one of the best luchadors going, and it felt like he was giving too much to the less experienced star to make this a genuine struggle.

There was little drama to the finish as Fénix was not going to lose less than a week away from the biggest match of his WWE career against Penta.

It might have been best to keep this shorter and tighter to sell that Prosper has more to learn before he can contest one of AAA's best.

Fénix def. Prosper by pinfall to retain the AAA World Cruiserweight Championship.

While the main roster has not always responded to Fénix, the NXT crowd was quickly chanting "Animo" for the champion.

In the men's locker room, Myles Borne and Tavion Heights talked strategy with NASCAR racer Sam Mayer joined by Hank Walker and Tank Ledger, who wanted the next tag title shot.

Kendal Grey arrived first with Wren Sinclair, promising the NXT women's champion was a fighting champion.

Kelani Jordan arrived followed by Zaria and Kali Armstrong, all promising victory at Heatwave.

Grayson Waller interrupted to talk up the talent in the arena before telling them that it was time for them to all let him talk.

Tony D'Angelo told Waller that he would fail like he always does. Cruz Montana arrived to declare himself a fighter not a talker, starting a brawl including security.

Zilla Fatu arrived late to take out his competition, raising the NXT Championship, while Grey and Wren held the NXT Women's, Women's North American and Women's Speed Championships high.

While the crowd popped big for Zilla and NXT got a nice final shot of possible winners standing tall, this was a mess that did no one any favors.

Waller has quickly lost steam due to the messy build of the NXT Championship match and looked like a chump in the chaos.

WrenQCC stood tall by the end, but most of the challengers got a forgettable 10 seconds to speak on a night that needed to solidify more stars.

Even if the goal is to sell fans on the "chaos" of NXT, this did not serve as a final exclamation mark before Heatwave. It was just the same-old NXT standard of overloading a segment without substance.

Grey threw shade at Liv Morgan, refusing to wait to defend her gold.

Waller called the women in the ring the 10%, referencing his recent line that these were the women ready for the main roster call-up.

Vic Joseph ran down the Heatwave card before the Championship Summit:

Women's North American and Speed Championship Unification: Zaria (c) vs. Wren Sinclair (c) vs. Kali Armstrong.

North American Championship: Myles Borne (c) vs. Jackson Drake.

NXT Tag Team Championships: Myles Borne and Tavion Height (c) vs. The Vanity Project's Brad Baylor and Ricky Smokes.

NXT Championship: Tony D'Angelo (c) vs. Grayson Waller vs. Cruz Montana vs. Zilla Fatu.

NXT Women's Championship: Kendal Grey (c) vs. Kelani Jordan.

The go-home show to Heatwave was, in a single word, underwhelming.

Beyond Nattie and Jaida Parker maximizing their limited minutes to sell their feud ending Submission match, nothing got a boost in hype from this show.

Kali Armstrong and Zaria delivered in the ring, but she may have unnecessarily complicated a simple story between Zaria and Wren Sinclair.

Rey Fénix and EK Prosper delivered an over-the-top main event that does not connect to anything on the PLE to come. The same can be said for the opening battle of Saquon Shugars and Dion Lennox.

The main hype for the night came from the main event chaos, and that was a mess that only showed that the main angles for Heatwave have been rushed.

articles.title: Astros Owner Jim Crane Retains Joe Espada For Rest Of Season Following GM Ouster
articles.summary: Houston Astros owner Jim Crane says manager Joe Espada will remain in the role for the remainder of the season.
articles.body: A day after parting ways with general manager Dana Brown, Houston Astros owner Jim Crane addressed the move and said manager Joe Espada will remain in the role for the remainder of the season. Before opening a three-game series against the Yankees on Tuesday, the Astros moved on from Brown, whose contract was set to expire at the end of the season. The team described the decision as mutual. Houston announced senior adviser Jeff Bagwell and assistant general managers Charles Cook, Gavin Dickey and Connor Huff will take over Brown’s responsibilities, while Crane will oversee baseball operations during the transition. "There’s no good time for any of that, you know, when you let someone go," Crane said outside the Houston clubhouse. "Just out of respect for Dana, we thought that was a time that would give him a little space to regroup. He’s a great talent. He’s been in the business a long time to get settled and to get back to work somewhere else." Brown was hired in January 2023 and succeeded James Click, who was fired six days after Houston won its second World Series title. "We worked together very closely for three and a half years," Espada said. "He gave me the opportunity to be manager of this team. It was tough. It was a tough conversation, but he was grateful for the opportunity and I’m grateful for our relationship and how we grind through this together, but it was emotional. It was a lot of emotions behind our conversation." Brown helped the Astros reach a seventh straight ALCS, which they lost in seven games to the Texas Rangers. Houston lost in a wild-card series to Detroit in 2024 and last season missed the playoffs for the first time since 2016 when it finished three games behind Seattle in the AL West and lost a tiebreaker with the Tigers for final wild-card spot. "Not everybody’s been able to do it, that’s a good run," Crane said. "We hope to keep that going. We had a little hiccup last year where we didn’t make the playoffs but we’re right there. I think some few adjustments we can get back to that and some good decisions. Certainly you got to keep working on it but the expectation that I have is that we’re in the playoffs every year. It’s hard to win every year, but to get there." The Astros began this year 20-31 but were only 5 1/2 games out of first place in a weak AL West on May 20. Houston (65-66) recovered to win 40 of its next 66 games through a 6-3 win over San Diego on Aug. 7 but entered Tuesday with nine losses in 14 games, including four to the Angels and A’s, though Crane said that performance did not influence his decision to dismiss Brown. "That didn’t have anything to do with it," Crane said. "We’re focused on winning the AL, winning the division and that’s our focus but that didn’t have anything to do with it." Espada was promoted from bench coach after the 2023 season when Dusty Baker retired. He helped the Astros recover from a 12-24 start to win their seventh AL West crown in eight seasons in 2024 and began Tuesday with a 240-214 record. "I don’t know where that got mixed up, but that’s the same answer I gave since the first of the year," Crane said. "We told him we’d deal with that at the end of the season and we’ve never changed that answer all year long." Before Crane addressed reporters for nearly 10 minutes, he met with Espada. "Focus on winning today, that’s how I left that," Espada said. "My responsibility is to lead this team. We have a very important stretch of games here. So I walk out of our office ready to go." Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: SEC joins Big Ten in banning pros from returning to college, includes basketball players
articles.summary: The rule bans players who have been drafted by NFL, NBA, or WNBA teams or listed on their rosters.
articles.body: The Southeastern Conference passed a rule Tuesday banning players who have been drafted by NFL, NBA or WNBA teams or listed on rosters in those leagues, joining the Big Ten in taking a strong stand against this month’s unexpected surge of pro players trying to return to college. The SEC’s rule differs from the one adopted by the Big Ten, which only included football in its decision released earlier in the day. Combined, it leaves little doubt about where the nation’s two biggest conferences stand in the wake of court orders that were allowing players who had been on pro rosters, then released, to return back to college. It puts LSU on notice. This week, Tigers coach Lane Kiffin added Dae’Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, a pair of undrafted players out of Mississippi who had tryouts in the NFL over the summer but were released by their teams during training camp.
